title: Coefficient naturality of the specified projection reverse arrow
statement: Use the ringed-topos module adjunction h^* ⊣ h_* and its canonical derived adjunction Lh^* ⊣ Rh_*, the derived tensor models, their K-flat comparison isomorphisms, and the complex comparison hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. Let E be an object of D(S), represented by a K-injective complex K with a fixed isomorphism E ≅ Q(K). Let F and G be bounded complexes of R-module sheaves, each supplied with a strict-perfect coefficient package, and let f:F → G be a cochain map. Write rho_F and rho_G for the specified reverse arrows of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], A(f)=1_(Rh_*E) tensor^L Q(f), and B(f)=Rh_*(1_E tensor^L Lh^*(Q(f))). Then B(f) followed by rho_G equals rho_F followed by A(f). The packages and bounds on the two complexes can be chosen independently.

proof.text: Fix the first complex K. The ordinary tensor pullback comparison is natural in the second complex: check equality after every coprojection of each total degree, and apply naturality of the ordinary tensor comparison. Inverting this square and taking adjuncts, naturality of the counit gives naturality of the tensor-adjunction total map t_F. For bounded strict-perfect coefficients these maps are isomorphisms by the tensor-adjunction invertibility theorem in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows].

proof.text: To prove naturality of a mixed tensor representative with first factor A, choose one flat-term K-flat resolution p:P → A from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The normalization equations defining the mixed representatives identify both of their pullbacks along Q(p) with r_R inverse followed by Q(p tensor 1). Naturality of r_R and functoriality of the total tensor give a commuting rectangular diagram. Cancel the invertible map induced by Q(p) to obtain the desired square. Apply this once over R and once over S. The canonical pullback theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] verifies that the pulled-back coefficient complexes are flat-term K-flat.

proof.text: The complex comparison maps for derived pullback and pushforward are the components of composites of natural transformations, hence natural. Combine their squares with the mixed-representative squares to obtain the two representative-isomorphism squares. Invert the naturality square for t_F using cancellation of an isomorphism; transport it through the representative squares. This gives exactly B(f) rho_G = rho_F A(f), since the specified reverse arrow is that transported inverse. No presentation of F or G is changed. Zero maps, zero complexes and rank-zero packages satisfy the same functoriality and cancellation equations.

theorem ringedProjectionFormulaInverse_naturality
    (F G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose JC (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (P : StrictPerfectCoefficientPackage _ F) (P' : StrictPerfectCoefficientPackage _ G)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ r : ℤ, r < a ∨ b < r → IsZero (F.X r))
    (hb' : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ r : ℤ, r < a ∨ b < r → IsZero (G.X r))
    (f : F ⟶ G) :
    RF.map (TS.map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom (𝟙 E) (LF.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map f)))) ≫
      (ringedProjectionFormulaArrows uInv uPush adj I c uStar hobj hmap LF epsilon hLF PR PS hPR
        hPS TR
      TS rR rS k V am RF eta hRF computeR computeL adjD canonicalAdj E K hK repE G P' hb').2 =
    (ringedProjectionFormulaArrows uInv uPush adj I c uStar hobj hmap LF epsilon hLF PR PS hPR hPS
      TR
      TS rR rS k V am RF eta hRF computeR computeL adjD canonicalAdj E K hK repE F P hb).2 ≫
      TR.map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (RF.obj E)) (DerivedCategory.Q.map f))
